evidence: src/application/services.ts: TaskManagementService has the private helpers requireProject, requireTask and requireUser, which hold each existence check in one place; addTask, assignTask, listTasks, markDone and getProject all use them.
src/application/services.ts: UserService and TaskManagementService both receive repositories and IdGenerator through constructor injection, so they use the same abstractions.
src/application/services.ts: listTasks throws ValidationError("Status filter must be one of: todo, in progress, done"), which hardcodes the domain's TaskStatus values. This is minor duplication.

src/application/services.ts: addTask passes `status: input.status as TaskStatus | undefined` without calling isTaskStatus, while listTasks does call isTaskStatus. Validation is applied unevenly but is not clearly duplicated.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is a single file, src/application/services.ts, and it covers one concern: application use cases for project, task and user management. It defines one port, IdGenerator, and two input DTOs (CreateTaskInput, ListTasksInput). Both services use the same abstractions: repositories and IdGenerator are injected through the constructor, and the domain factories and transitions do the actual work (createProject, createTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, createUser). Existence checks are kept in one place each, in the private helpers requireProject, requireTask and requireUser, and every use case calls them. I found no split into unrelated concerns and no bypass of the module's own abstractions.

Two small inconsistencies are worth noting, but neither is strong enough to fail the rule:
(1) The listTasks error message hardcodes the allowed statuses ("todo, in progress, done"). This repeats the TaskStatus set from the domain instead of deriving it.
(2) addTask casts input.status to TaskStatus without calling isTaskStatus, while listTasks does validate with isTaskStatus. Status validation is applied unevenly at the application boundary, although createTask may validate it in the domain.
